title: Guest Accounting Computation Note: Amount of the Elite Breakfast Credit on a Guest Folio
content:
An Ashbury Rewards elite breakfast credit on Guest Folios is an amount set against one breakfast line, and a credit posted later by guest services goes against one particular breakfast line of the stay.

## Which line

Guest services posts a missed credit for the breakfast line of the most recent morning of the stay on which a breakfast was charged, the largest breakfast line of that morning when it carries several, with the reason that the elite benefit was not applied and within the brand's desk adjustment limit; a missed credit on an earlier morning is referred to the hotel as a billing dispute, because the outlet's own records of that morning are needed.

## The amount

The elite breakfast credit for one breakfast line is the lower of that line's amount and the morning's breakfast allowance. The morning's breakfast allowance is the brand's elite breakfast credit per person times the brand's persons covered. The credit is rounded half up to the cent and only at the end.

Put as a definition: the credit is the smaller of two amounts — the breakfast line as charged, and the allowance for that morning — and the allowance is the per-person figure taken as many times as there are persons covered. Rounding to the cent is done once, on the credit itself, never on an intermediate figure.

| Input | Where it is read |
|---|---|
| The breakfast line | The folio line charged at the breakfast outlet: the largest such line of the most recent morning of the stay on which a breakfast was charged |
| The brand's elite breakfast credit per person | The brand's figure in the breakfast entitlement grid |
| The brand's persons covered | The brand's figure in the breakfast entitlement grid |

## Worked example (hypothetical figures)

Inputs: a brand credit per person of $30.00 and persons covered of 2; the stay's breakfasts were charged on the mornings of 14, 15 and 16 June, and 16 June carries two breakfast lines, $41.00 and $27.50.

1. The most recent morning with a breakfast charged is 16 June; its largest breakfast line is $41.00.
2. The morning's breakfast allowance is $30.00 times 2, that is $60.00.
3. The credit is the lower of $41.00 and $60.00: **$41.00**.

Had the 16 June line been $72.00, the credit would have been the allowance of **$60.00**. A credit said to be missing from the morning of 14 June is an earlier morning, and is referred to the hotel as a billing dispute.

## Points of judgement

- **Several breakfast lines on the last morning.** The credit goes to the largest of them.
- **Equal amounts.** Where the breakfast line equals the allowance, the credit is that amount.
- **Rounding.** Half up, to the cent, at the end only.
